description: Shared canonical dictionary v1.1 for the parser, the router and scoring. 8 staged analytes plus not-staged numeric, qualitative and descriptive analytes across the cbc, metabolic, renal, hepatic, thyroid and urinalysis panels. type gives the scoring mechanism: staged means the analyte is banded by the cut-offs in CLINICAL_RULES (seven guideline-anchored; creatinine's cut-offs are project-defined); not_staged means it is scored against the printed range or the expected-value rule, or is not scored (descriptive). Where a severity came from is recorded per row by range_basis in Contract B, not by type.
matching_rules: Names are compared after normalization: lowercase, punctuation replaced by spaces, whitespace collapsed.
Try the report section's section_aliases first, then an exact whole-name alias match. Use fuzzy matching only when there is no exact match.
Aliases of 3 characters or fewer (K, Na, Hb, TG, Eos ...) match exactly only; never fuzzy-match them.
Where one alias is contained in a longer alias of another code (Hemoglobin vs Hemoglobin A1c, Cholesterol vs LDL Cholesterol, MCH vs MCHC), the longer, exact match wins.

Units: a reported unit is accepted as-is only if it equals standard_unit or one of unit_aliases after normalization (lowercase, micro sign to u, superscript 2 to 2, spaces removed). unit_aliases are numerically identical spellings only.
Real unit conversions (g/L to g/dL, mmol/L to mg/dL and so on) are listed in unit_conversions.json and applied by the parser before scoring. The scoring module still compares units strictly.
Analytes with standard_unit null are dimensionless or non-numeric; they accept a missing unit.
result_kind: numeric (scored from a value and a range), qualitative (scored with the expected_values rule), descriptive (stored, never scored).

default_ref_interval is used only when the report prints no range for a numeric analyte. An interval is kept only when the published sources checked agree on one adult interval and it is cited (status cited; source is a citation with a URL and an access date). Otherwise it is null and default_ref_reason records why (ticket ML-04).
plausible_range is a project-defined sanity bound used for OCR confidence checks, not a clinical reference.
The parser must emit standard_unit exactly (scoring compares units strictly for staged analytes).
Rows with no dictionary match are emitted with canonical_code null in Contract A and enter Contract B as 'unknown_unmapped' (scored only when the lab printed its own range).

default_ref_reason records why a numeric lab-range analyte has no default (ML-04); such a row is scored only against a printed range and is indeterminate otherwise. A row scored against a default carries range_basis dictionary_default in Contract B.
